Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data Scientist with experience building and operationalizing forecasting, churn propensity and experimentation solutions using Python, SQL and cloud data tools. Developed a scheduled forecasting workflow in Vertex AI Workbench and weekly batch scoring in BigQuery, with measurable business outcomes. MSc in Statistics with a foundation in modelling uncertainty and experimental design. Building production software engineering practices, including Docker and automated tests.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and analysis: Python, SQL, R
Machine learning: LightGBM, XGBoost, feature engineering, SHAP, scikit-learn, statsmodels
Data and cloud: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt
Software and testing: Docker, Streamlit, pytest, unit testing
Other: Looker, R Markdown

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Data Scientist | Thistlebox | 2022–Present
- Developed a weekly recipe-demand forecasting workflow for orders by recipe and region, forecasting six weeks ahead using LightGBM and calendar, price and menu-position features.
- Scheduled the forecasting notebook in Vertex AI Workbench to write forecasts to BigQuery for operational use in Looker; improved WAPE from 23% to 14%, with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste.
- Built a churn propensity model using XGBoost; weekly batch scoring in BigQuery supports retention offers to top-decile customers. A 10% holdout validation showed churn was 2.1 percentage points lower in the treated group.
- Built a Streamlit application for planning and analysing sequential A/B tests, used by approximately 25 people in product and growth. Wrote the app and its Dockerfile; the data platform team handles deployment to Cloud Run.
- Began writing pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code in 2025; coverage is approximately 60%.
- Delivered the internal “Stats for PMs” training three times.

Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail | 2020–2022
- Segmented customers and analysed tariffs using R and SQL.
- Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team approximately two days each month.

EDUCATION
MSc Statistics
- Dissertation on Bayesian hierarchical models.
- Foundation in experimental design and modelling uncertainty.

ADDITIONAL PROJECT
Image Classification Course Project | 2025
- Fine-tuned a small CNN on a public food-images dataset, achieving approximately 80% accuracy. Learning project completed as part of an online deep learning course.
- Technologies: PyTorch, torchvision, Google Colab.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured and professionally written. It uses strong evidence-based bullets with metrics such as WAPE improvement from 23% to 14%, an estimated 9% food-waste reduction, a 2.1-percentage-point churn difference and approximately 25 internal users. The document presents the candidate's progression from analyst to data scientist effectively and accurately distinguishes production use from personal learning. The strongest content is the forecasting, churn and experimentation experience. The main content limitation is not writing quality but the candidate's substantial experience gap against this specifically senior/production-oriented Machine Learning Engineer role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, plain text formatting, readable dates and searchable technical keywords including Python, SQL, LightGBM, XGBoost, feature engineering, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Docker, Streamlit, pytest, dbt and unit testing. The document should parse well, but the literal [EMAIL], [PHONE] and [LINKEDIN] placeholders must be replaced before submission. AI screening probability is moderate-to-low for this vacancy because the CV does not contain supported evidence for chat assistants, RAG, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, MLflow, Kubeflow, Airflow or equivalent LLM observability. These are genuine experience gaps rather than keywords that should be added without evidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with Python-based machine learning, feature engineering, batch scoring, cloud data work, experimentation and measurable business impact. GCP-related experience is shown through BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench, and the candidate demonstrates emerging software-engineering practice through Docker and pytest. Internal training supports the company's learning and knowledge-sharing culture. However, the document does not establish the advertised profile of an ML Engineer with at least four years of production ML engineering experience. The candidate's experience is as a Data Scientist, with scheduled notebooks and SQL batch scoring rather than self-managed model APIs or serving infrastructure. There is also no evidence of chat assistants, RAG, language-model fine-tuning, model monitoring, data versioning or named MLOps platforms. The MSc in Statistics is relevant to modelling and experimentation but does not clearly match the stated degree preference for machine learning, computer science or a related engineering field.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: Before submitting, replace [EMAIL], [PHONE] and [LINKEDIN] in the header with the candidate's actual contact details and a working LinkedIn URL if available.

MINOR ACCURACY/ALIGNMENT IMPROVEMENT: In the Professional Summary, replace “experience building and operationalizing forecasting, churn propensity and experimentation solutions” with “experience building and putting forecasting, churn propensity and experimentation solutions into operational use through scheduled batch workflows.” This more precisely reflects the documented implementation: a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook, BigQuery batch scoring and platform-managed Cloud Run deployment, without implying that the candidate personally built model-serving infrastructure.

MINOR ATS IMPROVEMENT: In the Thistlebox experience section, revise the forecasting bullet to explicitly include “scheduled batch workflow” and retain the existing tools, for example: “Developed and scheduled a weekly batch forecasting workflow in Vertex AI Workbench using LightGBM, writing six-week-ahead recipe-and-region forecasts to BigQuery for operational use in Looker.” This consolidates the strongest supported production and orchestration terminology without adding unsupported MLOps claims.

MINOR COMPLETENESS IMPROVEMENT: In the Thistlebox experience section, revise the churn bullet to include dbt because it is supported by the candidate's portfolio: “Built an XGBoost churn propensity model with feature engineering and SHAP analysis; weekly batch scores were written and used in BigQuery/dbt workflows to target retention offers to top-decile customers.” Only retain “dbt workflows” if dbt was actually part of this specific churn workflow; otherwise leave the current wording unchanged.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, concise, professionally structured, and uses credible quantified outcomes. The strongest evidence is the forecasting work: WAPE improved from 23% to 14% and estimated food waste reduction was 9%. The document also accurately distinguishes scheduled batch workflows from full API deployment, which supports credibility. However, the two forecasting bullets substantially repeat each other, the strongest churn result from the candidate material is omitted, and the document does not clearly distinguish production-adjacent delivery from production software engineering. The MSc, internal training, testing work, and practical projects provide useful context for a transition toward machine learning engineering.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly section headings, simple text formatting, standard bullet points, and relevant keywords including Python, SQL, LightGBM, XGBoost, feature engineering, SHAP, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Docker, Streamlit, pytest, and dbt. Its ATS match is limited by the absence of several job-specific terms that the candidate's material can support, especially dbt Cloud Scheduler, scheduled notebook orchestration, batch scoring, Cloud Run, and the quantified churn validation result. It should not add unsupported tools such as MLflow, Airflow, Kubernetes, model monitoring, data versioning, RAG, or chat assistants. The visible [EMAIL], [PHONE], and [LINKEDIN] placeholders must be replaced before submission because they reduce professionalism and may interfere with contact-field parsing. Estimated AI screening probability: moderate, approximately 55–65%, mainly because several must-have requirements are genuine candidate gaps rather than CV wording problems.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a credible match for a junior or transition-level machine learning engineering profile involving batch ML workflows. It shows Python, GCP-related tools through BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench, feature engineering, scheduled scoring, cloud-adjacent delivery, Docker, testing, and business-facing model use. The forecasting and churn projects also demonstrate ownership and practical outcomes relevant to building ML systems for operational teams. The match is substantially weaker for this specific role because the candidate's material does not show chat assistants, retrieval-augmented generation, language models, model serving performed personally, monitoring, data versioning, or four years as a machine learning engineer. The candidate has four years of relevant data science/data analysis experience from 2022 to present, but not four years in the advertised MLE title or scope. The MSc in Statistics is relevant to modelling and experimentation but is not clearly a degree in machine learning, computer science, or engineering. The CV provides some evidence of learning and knowledge sharing through the “Stats for PMs” training, but it does not need to claim unsupported company-culture traits.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL:
1. In the contact-information line at the top of the CV, replace “[EMAIL]”, “[PHONE]”, and “[LINKEDIN]” with the candidate’s actual email address, phone number, and LinkedIn URL before submission. Do not leave placeholders in the final document.

2. In the Professional Experience section under Thistlebox, remove the repeated forecasting bullet or merge the two bullets into one stronger bullet. For example: “Developed and scheduled a weekly six-week-ahead forecasting workflow in Vertex AI Workbench using LightGBM, writing recipe-and-region forecasts to BigQuery for operational use in Looker; improved WAPE from 23% to 14% and achieved an estimated 9% reduction in food waste.” This preserves the operational-use evidence without repeating the scheduling and BigQuery details.

3. In the Thistlebox experience section, strengthen the churn bullet with the supported validation outcome from the candidate material: “Built an XGBoost churn propensity model with feature engineering and SHAP analysis; weekly scores were written to BigQuery and used in dbt workflows to target retention offers to top-decile customers, with a 10% holdout showing a 2.1-percentage-point reduction in churn in the treated group.” Do not describe this as API serving or causal proof beyond the stated holdout result.

4. In the Technical Skills section, make the supported orchestration experience more explicit without adding unsupported tools. Change “Data and cloud: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt” to “Data, cloud and orchestration: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench scheduled notebooks, dbt, dbt Cloud Scheduler.” This uses the candidate’s actual working environment and improves keyword alignment with the orchestration requirement.

MINOR:
5. In the Professional Summary, make the production-scope distinction precise. Replace “building and putting forecasting, churn propensity and experimentation solutions into operational use through scheduled batch workflows” with “building and operationalising forecasting, churn propensity and experimentation solutions through scheduled batch workflows.” This is more concise and avoids implying that the candidate personally built a model-serving API.

6. In the Thistlebox experience section, change “the data platform team handles deployment to Cloud Run” to “packaged the Streamlit application in Docker for deployment to Cloud Run by the data platform team.” This gives the CV a stronger software-engineering keyword while accurately preserving the candidate’s limited deployment ownership.

7. In the Skills section, retain “pytest” and “unit testing,” but make the scope explicit: “pytest, unit testing of forecasting feature code.” This prevents the testing entry from implying broad production test ownership beyond the approximately 60% coverage described in the experience section.

8. In the Additional Project section, retain the “Learning project” wording and do not present PyTorch or CNN work as production machine learning experience. The current labelling is appropriately honest and should be preserved.

In particular, the CV appropriately does not claim API model serving, Kubernetes, MLflow, Airflow, monitoring, data versioning, chat assistants, or RAG.

The candidate has shipped scheduled batch ML workflows into operational use, but the supplied information does not establish API-based model serving or ownership of deployment infrastructure. critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is ATS-friendly overall: it uses conventional headings, simple text formatting, standard technology names and readable bullet points. The candidate's material does not show those requirements. The candidate has not personally deployed a model as an API, and the available information does not show model monitoring, data versioning, language-model work, text-dataset preparation, or the requested MLOps platforms. The MSc in Statistics is relevant quantitative education but is not an exact match for a degree in machine learning, computer science or engineering. The CV should present the existing experience strongly and accurately without implying unsupported production-engineering or generative-AI experience.
